outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records show both modes passed 40 of 40 testcases, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The parallel run had a real coordination defect around shared deliverable writes, but the root observed it, interrupted the children, reconciled the source tree, and reverified before final delivery. The serial run solved the same behavioral problem alone with no shared-writer episode.
parallel_contributors: Root-led black-box probing and final reconciliation produced a correct deliverable despite child-written duplicate files.
The retained parallel pattern was adverse process overhead, not an outcome-differential failure.
serial_contributors: Single-agent probing, implementation, cargo/rustc checks, direct comparison, and fuzzing produced the same official pass without shared-state conflict.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The final module layouts differed: parallel ended with `src/parser.rs`, `src/validation.rs`, and `src/path_utils.rs`, while serial used `src/url_parser/{parser,validate,path}.rs`.
Serial performed a 2,000-case fuzz pass; parallel performed a smaller final comparison after resolving child interference.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process episode
